title: CNC Programming and Operation; Intermediate Mill
description: This Intermediate CNC Mill course focuses on tool path programming using word address format, coordinate systems, cutter compensation using multiple D values and advanced canned cycles. Intermediate mill programming will utilize subprograms, multiple work coordinate systems and probe macros, as well as program entry, editing, simulation and advanced machine controller functions. Indexable tool insert selection, thread milling and Unified National thread form classes and measurement will also be included in this course.
outcomes: Demonstrate the set up and advanced operation of vertical machining centers.
Create advanced word-address programs to successfully construct projects using vertical machining centers.
objectives: Prepare and interpret programs for CNC lathes
Demonstrate the controls and functions of CNC controllers.
Prepare and interpret programs for CNC mills.
Verify mill programs with PC based solid modeling software.
Explain single point threading and measurement procedures for Unified threads.
Describe carbide insert ANSI designations, wear characteristics and applications.

assignments: Lab projects demonstrating mastery of skills using CNC machines, simulators and verification software covered in this course.
Take home worksheets involving cartesian coordinate calculations.
